issue.title: incorrect format `asTime` for postgres fields `timestamp with time zone`

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
### What steps will reproduce the problem?

formatter->defaultTimeZone = 'UTC'
formatter->timeZone = 'Etc/GMT-3'
formatter->timeFormat = 'php:H:i:s'

after version 2.0.11, incorrect format `asTime` for postgres fields `timestamp with time zone`
#13343
```php
$time = '16:22:00.44297+03';
echo Yii::$app->formatter->asTime($time);
````
### What is the expected result?
'16:22:00'
### What do you get instead?
'13:22:00'

### Additional info

| Q                | A
| ---------------- | ---
| Yii version      | 2.0.13.1
| PHP version      | 7.0.*
| Operating system | ubuntu 16.04

issue.title: SchemaTest fails with 'pgsql' driver

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body:
<!--
Please use this issue tracker for bugs and feature requests only. In case you need support please use one of
Yii communities listed at https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/wiki/communities
-->

I just study unit testing and stumbled upon next situation:

### What steps will reproduce the problem?

`./vendor/bin/phpunit -v --filter testColumnSchema tests/framework/db/pgsql/SchemaTest.php`

### What is the expected result?

```
PHPUnit 4.8.34 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.

Runtime:        PHP 7.2.14-1+ubuntu18.04.1+deb.sury.org+1 with Xdebug 2.6.1
Configuration:  /var/www/yii2.test/phpunit.xml.dist

..

Time: 568 ms, Memory: 6.00MB

OK (2 tests, 228 assertions)
```

### What do you get instead?

```
Runtime:        PHP 7.2.14-1+ubuntu18.04.1+deb.sury.org+1 with Xdebug 2.6.1
Configuration:  /var/www/yii2.test/phpunit.xml.dist

F.

You should really fix these slow tests (>500ms)...
 1. 504ms to run yiiunit\framework\db\pgsql\SchemaTest:testColumnSchema


Time: 918 ms, Memory: 6.00MB

There was 1 failure:

1) yiiunit\framework\db\pgsql\SchemaTest::testColumnSchema
defaultValue of column ts_default is expected to be an object but it is not.
Failed asserting that 'CURRENT_TIMESTAMP' is of type "object".

/var/www/yii2.test/tests/framework/db/SchemaTest.php:519
/var/www/yii2.test/vendor/phpunit/phpunit/phpunit:52

FAILURES!
Tests: 2, Assertions: 152, Failures: 1.
```

### Additional info

| Q                | A
| ---------------- | ---
| Yii version      | master
| PHP version      | 7.2.14-1+ubuntu18.04.1+deb.sury.org+1 (cli) (built: Jan 13 2019 10:05:45) ( NTS )
| Operating system | Linux farm 4.15.0-43-generic #46-Ubuntu SMP Thu Dec 6 14:45:28 UTC 2018 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
| PosgreSQL | PostgreSQL 10.6 (Ubuntu 10.6-0ubuntu0.18.04.1) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Ubuntu 7.3.0-16ubuntu3) 7.3.0, 64-bit

Possible solution:
```
if ($connection->getDriverName() !== 'pgsql') {
    $this->assertInternalType('object', $column->defaultValue, "defaultValue of column $name is expected to be an object but it is not.");
    $this->assertEquals((string)$expected['defaultValue'], (string)$column->defaultValue, "defaultValue of column $name does not match.");
} else {
    $this->assertInternalType('string', $column->defaultValue, "defaultValue of column $name is expected to be an object but it is not.");
    $this->assertEquals((string)$expected['defaultValue'], 'now()', "defaultValue of column $name does not match.");
}
```

body:
Why can't we just adapt the tests to new conditions? Something like this:

Should we have separate tests for Postgres 9.x and Postgres 10.x versions?

body: Maybe it's better to make `Expression` from any not null `defaultValue` on `date/time` columns?

@samdark for some people - definetly. But I hope there are not so many ones with `defaultValue='2019-10-16'` or any other constant date or time.

On the other hand, Yii has  [`ActiveRecord::loadDefaultValues`](https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/74c6797a4113f972a69aa30b36d1d0f3db7f9d5c/framework/db/ActiveRecord.php#L116) and code like `$model->loadDefaultValues(); $model->save();` is not expected to throw "ERROR:  invalid input syntax for type date: "CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"". Currently [`now()`](https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/74c6797a4113f972a69aa30b36d1d0f3db7f9d5c/framework/db/pgsql/Schema.php#L545) is converted to `Expression` and doesn't produce errors while usage of [13 other](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-datetime.html#FUNCTIONS-DATETIME-CURRENT) standard functions leads to an exception on insert. Checking all of them is not a big deal, just a bit lengthy and makes wonder "what do we do with [MariaDB's](https://mariadb.com/kb/en/library/create-table/#invisible) 'NOW() + INTERVAL 1 YEAR'?".
Right. Then your solution makes sense.
This problem is still present in pgsql v. 10.14, what would be the best way to solve it?
